  PUBLIC COMMENT RULES:

 “(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
 (a) Every agenda for regular meetings shall provide an opportunity for members of the
 public to directly address the legislative body on any item of interest to the public, before
 or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter
 jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action shall be taken on any item not
 appearing on the agenda unless the action is otherwise authorized by subdivision (b) of
 Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

 (b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
 that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
 limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
 each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
 time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
 the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-
 English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
 a local agency.”

 In furtherance of Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act, the public is allotted to speak a total
 of three (3) minutes on the entirety of the Consent Calendar, with two (2) minutes on
 Public Hearing, and, if desired, an additional two (2) minutes on items not on the agenda
 that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. As specified in the Brown
 Act, a speaker utilizing a translator will receive twice the amount of time specified.

 Open and Invitation Survey
  4,500 SURVEYS
  Statistically Valid (Invitation Survey)
  Paper surveys were mailed to a systematic random sample of residential  & 4,500 POSTCARDS MAILED
  addresses in the City Palmdale, with the option to complete online through
  password protected website (1 response per household). The survey was also
  available online in Spanish. After initial invites were delivered, additional
  reminder postcards were sent, and phone calls were made to survey recipients
  to help encourage responses. In total, 227 invitation surveys were completed,
  yielding a +/-6.5% Margin of Error (MOE) at a 95% confidence level, indicating a

  1,301
  successful statistically valid survey effort. Acceptable margin of error used by
  most survey researchers usually falls between 4% and 8% at the 95%
  confidence level.

  227  Invitation surveys completed
  +/- 6.5% Margin of Error
  Open Link Survey

  scope and outreach of the survey effort. This Open Link Survey was promoted
  through multiple social media posts, email distribution lists, and QR codes were
  posted at all parks and recreation facilities. Targeted outreach was also done to
  reach youth in the area.

SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY AND QUARTERLY
  INVESTMENT ACTIVITY REPORTS FOR SEPTEMBER 2023

ISSUE
Receive and file the monthly and quarterly investment activity reports for September
2023.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the monthly and quarterly
investment activity reports for the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for
September 2023.

BACKGROUND
Pursuant to Section 16 of the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency Investment
Policy, the City Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on
investments to the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The
reports shall detail the type of investment, name of the issuer, purchase date, date of
maturity, amount of deposit, and rate of interest. This information shall be provided for
all City and Successor Agency pooled investments, as well as for Certificates of
Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts, and
Community Facilities District accounts, which are managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly and quarterly reports provide a synopsis of the investment activity for the
City of Palmdale and Successor Agency. The reports provide information on assets,
allocations, average maturities, yields, and book valuations. The interest rates
presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this report.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable sources of market prices.

Re: Monthly and Quarterly Reports on Investments
November 1, 2023
Page 2

DISCUSSION
Compliance with Investment Policy

For September, the invested portfolio amount for the City of Palmdale totaled
$305,065,778, a decrease of $34,305 from the previous month, and an increase of
$17,170,826 in comparison to last year. The monthly decrease is the result of
operational expenditures paid during the month.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of September was $7,915,579. The
balance increased by $10,834 from last month due to earned interest during the month.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities, and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entities’ investment policies to 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements; and
3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on is providing liquidity to measure up
to the City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance
Division is currently investing in two pooled funds, Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF)
and California Asset Management Program (CAMP). These are intended for daily
operational activities and used for economic uncertainties and maintenance needs. The
pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City and Successor Agency
meet cash flow requirements.

The total LAIF balance for the City of Palmdale at the end of September is $132,457,024,
with no changes compared to the prior month.

Successor Agency LAIF balance at the end of September was $7,024,790. No changes
compared to the prior month.

CAMP’s balance for City of Palmdale at the end of September was $262,895 compared
to August balance of $261,701. The slight increase is due to interest earned during the
month.

Diversity

The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual financial
institutions.

The City of Palmdale and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-073, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale to transfer unclaimed checks from their respective funds to the general fund
pursuant to California Government Code Section 50050-50057.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-073, a
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Palmdale to transfer unclaimed checks from
their respective funds to the general fund pursuant to California Government Code
Section 50050-50057.

BACKGROUND

Section 50050-50057 of the California Government Code states that “Except as
otherwise provided by law, money, excluding restitution to victims, that is not the
property of a local agency that remains unclaimed in its treasury or in the official custody
of its officers for three years is the property of the local agency after notice if not claimed
or if no verified complaint is filed and served. At any time after the expiration of the three-
year period, the treasurer of the local agency may cause a notice to be published once
a week for two successive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation published in the
local agency. At the expiration of the three-year period, money representing restitution
collected on behalf of victims shall be deposited into the Restitution Fund or used by the
local agency for purposes of victim services.

DISCUSSION

The City Treasurer desires to follow the guidelines set by California Government Code
Section 50053 and the policy set forth by this department in relation to this section.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-073
November 1, 2023
Page 2

Section 50053 states “When any such money becomes the property of a local agency
and is in a special fund, the legislative body may transfer it to the general fund.” The
total combined number of unclaimed checks for the three-year period ending June 30,
2023, is $9,375.91.

FISCAL IMPACT
The total combined number of unclaimed checks for the three-year period ending June

General Fund.

ISSUE
Approve Agreement with TruePoint Solutions, LLC to provide long-term support
services for Accela land use, plan review, permitting, and inspection tracking system for
a not-to-exceed amount of $396,000 for a term of three (3) years with the option to
extend by two additional terms of one (1) year each.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement A-8569 with TruePoint Solutions, LLC, to provide long-term
  support services for Accela land use, plan review, permitting, and inspection
  tracking system for a not-to-exceed amount of $396,000 for a term of three (3)
  years with the option to extend by two additional terms of one (1) year each; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement A-8569 with
  TruePoint Solutions, LLC., including any non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
In an effort to streamline and improve the City’s ability to process, review, and track
online permit applications and payments, the City partnered with TruePoint, LLC, in
December 2021 to implement Accela, a Land Use, Plan Review, Permitting, and
Inspection Tracking System. The software was successfully launched in July 2023, and
staff have worked with TruePoint Solutions to provide support and training to both
internal and external users. The existing agreement included implementation services
and support services and is set to expire in December 2023.

The Accela Land Use, Permitting, and Tracking system was launched in July 2023, and
is no longer in the implementation phase; however, ongoing support is needed to ensure
the system’s long-term stability and success. This will help guarantee the best experience
for our staff, contractors, and members of the public who rely on this application daily.

refresher courses for both new and existing staff members. This will help them stay
updated with all the latest changes and features in Accela. The requested funds will cover

ISSUE
Approve cooperative agreement with the County of Los Angeles for PN 847A, Arterial
Road Rehabilitation Project, for $1,300,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  A. Approve cooperative agreement with the County of Los Angeles for PN 847A,
  Arterial Road Rehabilitation Project, for $1,300,000; and,
  B. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Cooperative Agreement
  No. A-8342 with the County of Los Angeles, including non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The City and Los Angeles County have shared jurisdiction along Palmdale Blvd. from
50th St. East to 75th St. East and 40th St. East from Ave. N to Ave. N-8. Project No.
847A, Arterial Road Rehabilitation Project estimated cost is Seven Million Eight Hundred
Thousand Dollars ($7,800,000). The City’s share is to be Six Million Five Hundred
Thousand Dollars ($6,500,000), and the County’s share is to be One Million Three
Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,300,000). It is anticipated this project will go out to bid in
Dec. 2023, and construction will start in late Spring 2024. It will take approximately 45
working days from the date the City issues the Notice to Proceed and is projected to be
completed by the end of Summer 2024.

DISCUSSION
To achieve the most effective results, the City and County propose to design and
construct improvements on Palmdale Blvd. from 50th St. East to 75th St. East, which
consists of full-depth reclamation with cement stabilization. This method consists of
pulverizing the existing hot mix asphalt layer and the underlying material, adding cement,
compacting it to create a six or nine-inch layer, and overlaying it with a new hot mix

ISSUE
Approve first amendment with U.S. National Corp dba Jimenez Painting Company to
increase contract price by $840,000 in an amount not to exceed $1,240,000 for the
remainder of the contract term through June 2027.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve first amendment for Agreement No. A-7972 with U.S. National Corp dba
  Jimenez Painting Company to increase contract price by $840,000 in an amount
  not to exceed $1,240,000, for the remainder of the contract term through June
  2027; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to execute the First Amendment to
  Agreement No. A-7972 with U.S. National Corp dba Jimenez Painting Company
  including non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The City released Invitation for Bid No. 22-004-3400 for As Needed Professional Painting
Services in April 2022 and awarded the contract to U.S. National Corp dba Jimenez
Painting Company in August 2022, in the total amount of $400,000 for a three-year term
with the option to extend for two additional terms of one year each (through FY 26/27). It
was estimated at that time that the services would cost approximately $80,000 per year.

However, to address citywide painting needs and deferred maintenance, the City
requested the contractor perform extra painting work during the first year of the contract.
This included the painting of fencing in twelve Landscape Assessment Districts, the
 Report to Mayor and City Council

Antelope Valley Country Club planter sign, handrails, gates, posts, fencing, and/or
pavilion ceilings and facia at five City parks (Domenic Massari, Foothill, Marie Kerr, South
Pelona Vista, and Best of the West Softball Complex), ticket booths and two train shelters
at Palmdale Transportation Center; interior trim of the Administration building, metal
staircase at Chimbole Cultural Center; safety markings in the Oasis/DryTown Water Park
parking lot, Civic Center, Poncitlan Square’s gazebo, brick features, trash receptable, and
light standards, and the preparation, priming, and graffiti coating for Public Art locations.
These additional services resulted in more than double the original annual cost
projections being spent in one year ($183,940).

In addition to the work noted above a large-scale project funded by Measure AV was
completed at Desert Sands Park to repaint the pavilion, grounds surfaces, and
concession and shop building exteriors totaling $196,105.

As a result of this work, the original contract amount was exhausted during the first year
of the agreement. Therefore, additional funds are required to continue contracting
painting services with U.S. National Corp.

DISCUSSION
The first amendment will increase the contract price with U.S. National Corp $840,000
for a revised total of $1,240,000 through the remaining two-year term plus the two
options to extend through Fiscal Year 26/27. The new contract total reflects the
continued need for painting services citywide through the full contract term. Based on
the increase, the average cost per year will be $210,000, with $25,000 of that being
allocated for Measure AV funded projects.

This increase allows for, but is not limited to, the painting and/or primer work on exterior
and interior surfaces, wooden and/or metal doors, building fascia and/or rafter tails,
window casing and security screening, City standard light poles, park infrastructure and
surfaces, wrought iron fencing (about 2,100 linear feet each year), backflow or irrigation
controller enclosures, and Public Art pieces and surfaces. These specialized services
contribute to the beautification of the City’s infrastructure, preserving and extending the
life of our assets.

FISCAL IMPACT
Sufficient funds for as needed professional painting services are budgeted in the following
accounts during the contract term: Facility Maintenance (10133005), Landscape

accounts.

ISSUE
Approve Final Parcel Map No. 83940 (located at Rancho Vista Blvd & Town Center Drive).

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  A. Approve Final Parcel Map No. 83940 (located at Rancho Vista Blvd. and Town
  Center Drive); and,

  B. Authorize the City Clerk to execute City Clerk’s Statement and Special
  Assessments Statement; and,

  C. Authorize the Acting City Surveyor to execute the City Surveyor’s Statement and
  file the map with the County Recorder.

BACKGROUND
Final Parcel Map No. 83940 is a 5-acre subdivision, legally creating three commercial
lots. All proposed lot sizes and dimensions comply with the City’s Zoning Ordinance. The
subject property is located at Rancho Vista Blvd and Town Center Drive. The applicant
for this final parcel map is Protea Senior Living Palmdale, LLC, a California Limited
Liability Company. This tentative parcel map was approved by the Planning Commission
on March 9, 2023 by Resolution No. PC-2023-006.

This final parcel map is consistent with the tentative parcel map and all final map
conditions of approval have been met. The Acting City Land Surveyor has reviewed the
final map for technical accuracy and verified it is compliant with the Subdivision Map Act.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE AGREEMENT FOR LEGAL SERVICES WITH HARPER &

ISSUE
Approve agreement for legal services with Harper & Burns, LLP, including appointing
William P. Curley, III, as City Attorney.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8599, for Legal Services with Harper & Burns, LLP,
  including the appointment of William P. Curley, III, as City Attorney.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8599
  with Harper & Burns, LLP, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.
BACKGROUND
At the October 18, 2023, closed session meeting, the City Council approved contracting
the firm of Harper & Burns, LLP, for City Attorney services, including appointing William
P. Curley, III, as the City Attorney.
DISCUSSION
The City Council conducted an extensive recruitment and interview process for City
Attorney services. It was determined that the firm of Harper & Burns, LLP, best suits the
City’s legal needs and has directed the preparation of an agreement for legal services.
The agreement is attached for your consideration.
The firms’ professionalism, long-standing services to other jurisdictions, depth and
breadth of education, and knowledge of municipal government matters, along with their
skills, ethics, and qualifications, will enable the firm to effectively meet challenges and
contribute positively to the future of Palmdale.
Harper & Burns, LLP provides general municipal legal services as well as a variety of
specialized services. Specialized services include, but are not limited to, litigation and
third-party litigation management, oversight and direction, financing arrangement advice

including bonds, community facility districts and tax, real estate acquisition or
disposition, developer-related services, and other special projects. Harper & Burns also

FISCAL IMPACT
Funds are budgeted and available in City Attorney accounts 10114001-701000 through

2023-24, based on a $40,000 monthly retainer, plus billable hours for special services
as outlined in Attachment 1. Actual amounts may vary based on caseload, ongoing
litigation, and City needs.

The parties hereto agree as follows:

  SECTION 1. RECITALS. This Agreement is made and entered into with respect to the
following facts:

  A. City has previously engaged the services of William P. Curley III to act as the Interim City
Attorney for the City and to perform all legal services requested in conjunction therewith by
agreement; and

  B. It is the desire of the parties hereto to rescind and terminate that previous agreement, and

  C. The Firm has agreed to provide legal services, in the time, manner, and for the

  SECTION 2. LEGAL SERVICES. The Firm shall perform the following legal services
for the City:

  A. The City Attorney is designated as William P. Curley III and the Assistant City Attorney
is designated as Alexandra M. Halfman. The City Attorney or the Assistant City Attorney shall
attend all meetings of the City Council unless excused by the City Manager; the City Attorney, or
designee, shall attend all Planning Commission meetings unless excused by the City Manager or
Community Development Director. All other Harper & Burns attorneys are designated as Deputy
City Attorneys.

  B. Provide legal advice and opinions on all matters affecting the City when requested by the
City Council, the City Manager, a department head, other members of City management as
designated by the City Manager, except when prevented from doing so by a legal conflict; and

  C. Attend other meetings of boards, commissions, committees, and staff members of the City
as directed by the City Council or City Manager; and

  D. Prepare resolutions and ordinances, review and approve as to legal form all City contracts,
agreements, and documents as requested and perform such other duties and responsibilities as set
forth in the Palmdale Municipal Code; and

   E. Undertake prosecution and litigation of violations of City ordinances as directed to do so

Council. At the outset of each matter of litigation (other than code violations), the City Attorney
shall cause a written estimated litigation budget, based on then known facts and information from
the other party, to be prepared and presented to the City Manager. The City Attorney and City
Manager (or City Manager’s designee) shall monitor the expenditures and provide updates to the
City Council (or City Manager), including cost revisions, at regular intervals to be determined on
a case-by-case basis; and

  G. The City Manager is hereby authorized to meet with the City Attorney to discuss service
and performance levels at any time during this Agreement, and to bind the attorneys to items
including, but not limited to, a schedule of regular office hours and standard response times to
service requests specialty projects, obtaining expert advice or services from third parties and any
action necessary or desirable for the health, safety and welfare of the City and its legal
representation. In addition, the City Attorney shall maintain a list of pending work assignments
and shall provide progress reports thereon to the City Manager as directed by the City Manager.

  H. The City Council shall retain the right to direct that attorneys other than the Firm perform
legal work for the City or any of its related entities but shall require the Firm and City Attorney to
oversee, manage and report on the third-party representation to the City Manager.

  I. The City Council shall interact respectfully with the City Attorney and the Firm and shall,
as professionally necessary or consistent with the civil norms, support the Firm and City Attorney
at all times.

that these activities be financed with the issuance of Lease Revenue Bonds (“Lease
Revenue Bonds”) by the Palmdale Financing Authority. This will allow the property to be
paid for over a longer term and preserve Measure AV fund balance for projects already
budgeted.

DISCUSSION
The City has the opportunity to purchase 56 acres of land along the 14 Freeway located
between Avenue Q and Palmdale Boulevard. The financing needed for this property,
including costs of acquisition, is approximately $18 million. Staff estimates that
approximately 50% of this property may be sold for development in the near future. Staff
is recommending that 50% of the property acquisition costs be funded with taxable
Lease Revenue Bonds, instead of tax-exempt Lease Revenue Bonds, to provide the

be required to pay off the Lease Revenue Bonds and could be recycled into funding
additional economic development projects or other City expenditures.

The City is also considering the acquisition of approximately 649 acres of property in
the Ritter Ranch specific plan. The financing needed for this property is approximately
$10.8 million. Staff is recommending that the property acquisition costs be funded with
tax-exempt Lease Revenue Bonds.

In addition, there are certain economic development projects in process, and staff
expect some up-front funding will be necessary. Staff is recommending that $5 million
be financed for this purpose, which will be funded with taxable Lease Revenue Bonds.
If not all of the funding is needed, the balance can be applied to other projects.

Finally, staff is recommending the refinancing of the Palmdale Financing Authority Lease
Revenue Bonds, Series 2012 (“2012 Bonds”). This refinancing is needed to free up
excess value needed to secure the leases for the Lease Revenue Bonds, since a large
portion of the property being acquired, or contributions made will not be used to secure
the leases necessary for the financing. There is a minor amount of negative savings
associated with the refunding of the 2012 Bonds due to current interest rates, but the
refunding is being undertaken for non-economic reasons — to access the excess value
associated with the leased property for the current financing. The City’s debt policy
allows for refinancing outstanding debt in order to realize the benefits of a debt
restructuring, and refinancing with negative savings requires additional approval of the
City Council.

Lease Revenue Bonds

Financing the acquisition price of the properties and the economic development projects
will be accomplished by the issuance of Lease Revenue Bonds by the Palmdale
Financing Authority (Authority). The City will lease property from the Authority, and the
City’s lease payments will secure the Authority Lease Revenue Bonds, as described
further below. The tax-exempt Lease Revenue Bonds are designated as Series 2023A
(“Series A Bonds”), and the taxable Lease Revenue Bonds are designated as Series
2023B (“Series B Bonds”).

This financing structure is similar to the Lease Revenue Bonds and Certificates of
Participation financings that the City has used for capital financing in the past. The City
formed the Palmdale Financing Authority in 2012 to assist in lease financings.

The financing requires a lease of assets from the Authority to the City. The City’s lease
payments to the Authority are used as a revenue stream to secure repayment of the
Lease Revenue Bonds. Because the City will not have title to the properties being
acquired until after the Lease Revenue Bonds are issued or doesn’t expect to retain title

Method of Sale

Under current market conditions, the City’s Municipal Advisor (Harrell & Company
Advisors) advised that it would be more cost-effective to sell the Lease Revenue Bonds
using a negotiated sale with one underwriter than a competitive bid. Selling a taxable
series of municipal bonds would be challenging under current conditions where the US
Treasury market (the benchmark for pricing taxable muni bonds) is so volatile. Because
both series need to be sold at the same time, and the possibility that there might not be
any bids on the taxable Lease Revenue Bonds, negotiating with one underwriter for the
purchase of both series is the best path for this issue.

The Municipal Advisor negotiated an underwriting proposal with Hilltop Securities. The
lead banker of this firm has underwritten most of the City’s financings in the last five
years and is familiar with the City’s finances.

Public Hearing

Government Code requires the City Council, as the governing body of the jurisdiction
where the facilities being financed are located, to hold a public hearing and make certain
findings before the Authority may approve a resolution authorizing the sale of the Lease
Revenue Bonds. The finding being made is that significant public benefits will arise from
the City’s issuance of the Lease Revenue Bonds to fund the property acquisition and

FISCAL IMPACT
Staff first considered using Measure AV fund balance to pay for the projects rather than
financing and determined that the long-term financing would have the least impact on
the City’s General Fund and Measure AV fund cash flow. This is critical to continuing to
use Measure AV fund balance and annual funding for public safety and other pay-as-
you-go projects.

Another factor in this decision was expected future funding needs for projects such as
the pool cover at Marie Kerr Park, Chimbole Center and Library improvements, and Dry
Town improvements. Given the costs involved, it is likely that these projects will also be
funded with lease revenue bonds, preserving Measure AV funding for pay-go projects.
In addition, many of the City’s prior financings will be paid in full in the next 10 years,
and the capacity to pay debt service from the General Fund will increase, providing a
funding source for some of the costs of these projects.

Staff prepared a long-term debt service projection, taking into account the maturity of
the existing City debt, the amount of any existing or new City debt that could be allocated
to other funds, and any reduction in the existing 2021 Lease Agreement for partial
redemption upon sale of the property securing that agreement (corner of Avenue M and
Sierra Highway).

Based on current interest rates, the effective interest rate for the Series A Bonds is
5.14% and the effective interest rate for the Series B Bonds is 6.87%. These rates are
approximately 1 percent higher than estimates from just last summer. Rates have been
affected by actual economic data, past and expected future Federal Reserve Board
actions, as well as a Federal government potential shutdown as the new deadline of
November 15 approaches for approval of a Federal budget for 2023-24.

Based on current market conditions, the par amount of the Series A Bonds is estimated
to be $26,295,000, issued with an original issue premium of $1,058,000, and will provide
total funding of $27,353,000.

The par amount of the Series B Bonds is estimated to be $14,965,000. The proceeds
from the Lease Revenue Bonds are estimated to be used as follows:

An original issue premium (as shown in the table above) is generated when investors in
tax-exempt bonds want to hedge against future higher interest rates and require a high
stated interest rate (such as 5.0%), but price the Series A Bonds to yield a lower current
market interest rate (such as 3.0%) and therefore pay the Authority more than 100% of
the face value of the Series A Bonds, resulting in a lower par amount of Series A Bonds
required to be issued. The lower par amount is offset by a higher interest rate, so this
pricing method has relatively little impact on the total debt service that the City will pay on
the Lease Revenue Bonds compared to if they were priced at 100% of the face value.
Taxable bonds such as the Series B Bonds are generally priced at 100% of the face value
but could be priced with premiums or discounts based on investor preference at the time
the Lease Revenue Bonds are sold.

As noted, the par amount of the Lease Revenue Bonds will be subject to prevailing market
conditions at the time of sale. Therefore, the City is requested to approve a not-to-exceed
par amount of $28,000,000 for Series A with an interest rate not to exceed 6% and a not-
to-exceed par amount of $16,000,000 for Series B with an interest rate not to exceed
7.5% to provide a reasonable cushion above the expected par amount should interest
rates fluctuate or if the Lease Revenue Bonds are priced without an original issue
premium based on investor preference at the time of sale. The amount of the Lease
Revenue Bonds issued will only be the amount necessary to finance the projects outlined
above, and pay the costs as shown above.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PALMDALE FINANCING AUTHORITY OF THE
  CITY OF PALMDALE AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF ITS
  PALMDALE FINANCING AUTHORITY (LOS ANGELES COUNTY,
  CALIFORNIA) LEASE REVENUE BONDS TO FINANCE THE
  ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN PROPERTY AND PROJECTS AND TO
  REFINANCE CERTAIN OUTSTANDING OBLIGATIONS, APPROVING
  THE FORM AND AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF RELATED
  DOCUMENTS AND APPROVING RELATED OFFICIAL ACTIONS

  WHEREAS, the Palmdale Financing Authority (the “Authority”) is a joint powers
authority duly organized and existing under and pursuant to that certain Joint Exercise of
Powers Agreement, dated as of September 26, 2012, by and between the City of
Palmdale (the “City”) and the Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale, and under the
provisions of Articles 1 through 4 (commencing with section 6500) of Chapter 5 of Division
7 of Title 1 of the California Government Code (the “Act”), and is authorized pursuant to
Article 4 of the Act (the “Bond Law”) to borrow money for the purpose of financing the
acquisition of bonds, notes and to issue bonds, notes or other evidences of indebtedness
or other agreements for all purposes permitted by the JPA Act and described in the
Agreement;

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale (the “City”) proposes to:

  (a) finance the cost of the acquisition of approximately 56 acres of real property,
of which 50% (the “Governmental Freeway Property”), will be used for governmental
purposes of the City and of which 50% (the “Non-Governmental Freeway Property”) is
expected to be sold for development,

  (b) finance the cost of the acquisition of real or other property which will be used
for governmental purposes of the City (the “Governmental Property”),

  (c) finance the cost of economic development projects in the City (the “Economic
Development Projects”), and

  (d) refund the outstanding Palmdale Financing Authority (Los Angeles County,
California) Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds, Series 2012 (the “2012 Bonds”);

  WHEREAS, it is proposed that the cost of the Governmental Freeway Property,
the Governmental Property and the refunding of the 2012 Bonds will be financed from the
proceeds of Palmdale Financing Authority (Los Angeles County, California) Lease
Revenue Bonds, Series 2023A (the “2023A Bonds”), to be issued by the Authority
pursuant to the provisions of Article 4 (commencing with section 6584) of the JPA Act (the
“Bond Law”), and pursuant to the terms of an indenture of trust, by and between the
Authority and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, as trustee (A-8549) (the
“Indenture”), and that the cost of the Non-Governmental Freeway Property and the
Economic Development Projects will be financed from the proceeds of Palmdale

  16001.03
 Financing Authority (Los Angeles County, California) Lease Revenue Bonds, Series
2023B (Federally Taxable) (the “2023B Bonds” and, with the 2023A Bonds, the “Bonds”),
to be issued by the Authority pursuant to the provisions of the Bond Law and the
Indenture;

  WHEREAS, in order to provide for the repayment of the Bonds, the City will lease
certain City-owned property and the sites thereof (collectively, the “Leased Property”) to
the Authority pursuant to a site and facility lease (A-8551) (the “Site and Facility Lease”)
and the Authority will lease the Leased Property back to the City pursuant to a lease
agreement (A-8550) (the “Lease Agreement”) under which the City will agree to make
lease payments to the Authority from moneys in the City’s General Fund and the City will
budget and appropriate sufficient amounts in each year to pay the lease payments which
will be equal to the scheduled principal of and interest on the Bonds;

  WHEREAS, the proposed form of a preliminary official statement (the “Preliminary
Official Statement”) describing the Bonds, to be used in connection with the marketing of
the Bonds, has been prepared and has been presented to the Authority;

  WHEREAS, Hilltop Securities Inc. (the “Underwriter”), has proposed to purchase
and underwrite the Bonds and has presented to the Authority and the City a form of bond
purchase agreement for the Bonds, to be entered into among the Authority, the City and
the Underwriter (A-8555) (the “Bond Purchase Agreement”);

  WHEREAS, the Board has duly considered such transactions and wishes at this
time to approve said transactions in the public interests of the Authority; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to section 5852.1 of the Government Code, which became
effective on January 1, 2018, by the enactment of Senate Bill 450, certain information
relating to the Bonds is set forth in Exhibit A attached to this Resolution, and such
information is hereby disclosed and made public;

  NOW, THEREFORE, it is hereby DECLARED and ORDERED, as follows:

  Section 1. Findings. The finding being made is that significant public benefits will
arise from the issuance of the Bonds to fund the property acquisition and other costs,
including demonstrable savings in effective interest rate, bond preparation and bond
issuance costs achieved by consolidating the assets being leased..

  Section 2. Issuance of Bonds. Pursuant to the Bond Law and the Indenture, the
Authority hereby authorizes the issuance of the Bonds. The Bonds shall be issued and
secured in accordance with the terms of and shall be in the form set forth in the Indenture
and subject to the parameters set forth in Section 7 below.

  Section 3. Approval of Indenture. The Board hereby approves the Indenture, in
the form on file with the Secretary, together with any changes therein or additions thereto
deemed advisable by the Chair, the Executive Director or the Treasurer of the Authority
(each, a “Designated Officer”), and the execution thereof by a Designated Officer shall be
conclusive evidence of such approval. The Designated Officers, each acting alone, are

  -2-
 hereby authorized and directed for and in the name and on behalf of the Authority to
execute the final form of the Indenture for and in the name of the Authority. The Board
hereby authorizes the delivery and performance of the Indenture. The dated date,
maturity date or dates, interest rate or rates, interest payment dates, denominations,
forms, registration privileges, manner of execution, place or places of payment, terms of
redemption, series designations and other terms of the Bonds shall be as provided in the
Indenture, as finally executed.

  Section 4. Approval of Site and Facility Lease. The Board hereby approves the
Site and Facility Lease, in the form on file with the Secretary, together with any changes
therein or additions thereto deemed advisable by any Designated Officer, and the
execution thereof by a Designated Officer shall be conclusive evidence of such approval.
The Designated Officers, each acting alone, are hereby authorized and directed for and
in the name and on behalf of the Authority to execute the final form of the Site and Facility
Lease for and in the name of the Authority. The Board hereby authorizes the delivery and
performance of the Site and Facility Lease.

  Section 5. Approval of Lease Agreement. The Board hereby approves the Lease
Agreement, in the form on file with the Secretary, together with any changes therein or
additions thereto deemed advisable by any Designated Officer, and the execution thereof
by a Designated Officer shall be conclusive evidence of the approval of any such changes
or additions. The Designated Officers, each acting alone, are hereby authorized and
directed for and in the name and on behalf of the Authority to execute the final form of the
Lease Agreement for and in the name of the Authority. The Board hereby authorizes the
delivery and performance of the Lease Agreement.

  Section 6. Approval of Escrow Agreement. The Board hereby approves an escrow
agreement, by and among the Authority, the City and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National
Association, as escrow agent, relating to the refunding of the 2012 Bonds (A-8552) (the
“Escrow Agreement”), in the form on file with the Secretary, together with any changes
therein or additions thereto deemed advisable by any Designated Officer, and the
execution thereof by a Designated Officer shall be conclusive evidence of the approval of
any such changes or additions. The Designated Officers, each acting alone, are hereby
authorized and directed for and in the name and on behalf of the Authority to execute the
final form of the Escrow Agreement for and in the name of the Authority. The Board hereby
authorizes the delivery and performance of the Escrow Agreement.

  Section 7. Approval of Termination Agreement. The Board hereby approves a
termination agreement, by and among the City, the Authority and the Trustee, providing
for the termination of the recorded documents relating to the 2012 Bonds (A-8562) (the
“Termination Agreement”), in the form on file with the Secretary. The Designated Officers,
each acting alone, are hereby authorized and directed to execute, for and in the name of
the Authority, the Termination Agreement in such form, together with any changes therein
or additions thereto deemed advisable by the Designated Officer executing the
Termination Agreement upon consultation with the Authority Counsel and Bond Counsel,
and the execution and delivery of the Termination Agreement by a Designated Officer
shall be conclusive evidence of the approval of any such changes or additions. The Board

  -3-
 hereby authorizes the delivery and performance by the Authority of the Termination
Agreement.

  Section 8. Sale of Bonds. The Board hereby approves the sale of the Bonds by
the Authority by negotiation with the Underwriter pursuant to the Bond Purchase
Agreement, in the form on file with the Secretary, together with such additions thereto
and changes therein as any Designated Officer shall deem necessary, desirable or
appropriate, and the execution thereof by a Designated Officer shall be conclusive
evidence of the approval of such additions and changes. The Designated Officers, each
acting alone, are hereby authorized and directed for and in the name and on behalf of the
Authority to execute the final form of the Bond Purchase Agreement for and in the name
of the Authority; provided that (a) with respect to the 2023A Bonds, (i) the amount of
Underwriter’s discount shall not be more than 0.60% of the par amount thereof, (ii) the
principal amount shall not be greater than $28,000,000, (iii) the true interest cost shall not
exceed 6.00% and (iv) the final maturity shall not extend beyond June 1, 2054, and (b)
with respect to the 2023B Bonds, (i) the amount of Underwriter’s discount shall not be
more than 0.75% of the par amount thereof, (ii) the principal amount shall not be greater
than $16,000,000, (iii) the true interest cost shall not exceed 7.50% and (iv) the final
maturity shall not extend beyond June 1, 2054.

  Section 9. Official Statement. The Board hereby approves, and hereby deems
nearly final within the meaning of Rule 15c2-12 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934
(the “Rule”), the Preliminary Official Statement in the form on file with the Secretary. The
Designated Officers, each acting alone, are hereby authorized and directed to execute
an appropriate certificate stating the Authority’s determination that the Preliminary Official
Statement is nearly final within the meaning of the Rule. Distribution of the Preliminary
Official Statement in connection with the sale of the Bonds is hereby approved. The
Designated Officers, each acting alone, are hereby authorized and directed, upon
consultation with Disclosure Counsel and counsel to the Authority, to approve any
changes in or additions to the Preliminary Official Statement deemed necessary or
desirable to bring it into the form of a final official statement (the “Final Official Statement”),
and the execution of the Final Official Statement by any Designated Officer shall be
conclusive evidence of approval of any such changes and additions. The Board hereby
authorizes the distribution of the Final Official Statement by the Underwriter. The Final
Official Statement shall be executed in the name and on behalf of the Authority by any of
the Designated Officers.

  Section 10. Official Actions. The Chairperson, the Executive Director, the
Treasurer, and the Secretary are each authorized and directed in the name and on behalf
of the Authority to make any and all assignments, and to execute any and all certificates
(including the Continuing Disclosure Certificate referenced in the Final Official
Statement), requisitions, agreements, notices, consents, instruments of conveyance,
warrants and other documents (including any agreement needed to obtain bond
insurance for the Bonds if in the judgment of the Treasurer/Auditor, upon consultation
with the Municipal Advisor, such insurance is cost effective), which they or any of them
deem necessary or appropriate in order to consummate the sale and issuance of the
Bonds and any of the other transactions contemplated by the documents approved
pursuant to this Resolution. Whenever in this Resolution any officer of the Authority is

  -4-
 authorized to execute or countersign any document or take any action, such execution,
countersigning or action may be taken on behalf of such officer by any person designated
by such officer to act on his or her behalf in the case such officer shall be absent or
unavailable.

  Section 11. Effective Date. This Resolution shall take effect from and after its
adoption.

  Section 12. The Authority Secretary shall certify to the adoption of this resolution.

The City and the Authority
The City of Palmdale (the “City”) was incorporated as a general law city on August 24, 1962. It became a
charter city in November 2009. The City encompasses approximately 104 square miles in an area of
northern Los Angeles County known as the Antelope Valley. The City is located approximately 60 miles
north of downtown Los Angeles. Neighboring communities include Santa Clarita and Lancaster (see “CITY
OF PALMDALE” herein).

The Authority is a joint exercise of powers authority organized and existing under and by virtue of the Joint
Exercise of Powers Act, constituting Articles 1 through 4 (commencing with Section 6500) of Chapter 5,
Division 7, Title 1 of the Government Code of the State of California (the “Joint Powers Act”). The City
and the Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale formed the Authority by the execution of a joint exercise
of powers agreement (“JPA Agreement”) dated September 26, 2012.

Under the JPA Agreement, the Authority is authorized to provide funds to acquire or construct and to
refinance public capital improvements, and to refinance obligations of its members issued for such
purposes, through the issuance of bonds in accordance with the Joint Powers Act.

The Authority is governed by a five-member Board of Directors which consists of all members of the City
Council. The Mayor serves as the Chair and the City Manager serves as the Executive Director of the
Authority.

 Purpose
The Series A Bonds are being issued to finance the acquisition of and improvement to certain land and
facilities, to refinance an existing lease by current refunding of the Authority’s outstanding Lease Revenue
Refunding Bonds, Series 2012 (the “2012 Bonds”), to capitalize a portion of the interest on the Series A
Bonds, to satisfy the Reserve Requirement for the Series A Bonds and to pay the costs incurred in
connection with the issuance of the Series A Bonds. The Series B Bonds are being issued to finance the
acquisition of and improvement to certain land and facilities, to capitalize a portion of the interest on the
Series B Bonds, to satisfy the Reserve Requirement for the Series B Bonds and to pay the costs incurred in
connection with the issuance of the Series B Bonds. See “THE FINANCING PLAN” herein.

Security and Sources of Repayment
The Bonds are secured under an Indenture of Trust, dated as of November 1, 2023, (the “Indenture”), by
and between the Authority and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, Los Angeles, California,
as trustee (the “Trustee”) (see “APPENDIX A - SUMMARY OF PRINCIPAL LEGAL DOCUMENTS” herein).

The Bonds are payable from the revenues pledged under the Indenture. The revenues consist primarily of
lease payments (the “Lease Payments”) to be made by the City to the Authority as the rental for real property
and improvements thereon (the “Leased Property”), from certain funds held under the Indenture and
investment earnings thereon and from net proceeds of insurance or condemnation awards with respect to
the Leased Property (collectively with the Lease Payments, the “Revenues”). See “THE LEASED
PROPERTY” herein.

Pursuant to a Site and Facility Lease, dated as of November 1, 2023 (the “Site Lease”), by and between the
Authority and the City, the City has leased the Leased Property to the Authority. The Authority has
subleased the Leased Property back to the City under a Lease Agreement, dated as of November 1, 2023,
by and between the City and the Authority (the “Lease Agreement”). The Lease Payments are to be made
by the City pursuant to the Lease Agreement.

Under the Lease Agreement and, subject to abatement, the City is required to make the Lease Payments
from legally available funds in amounts calculated to be sufficient to pay principal of and interest on the
Bonds when due. The City has covenanted in the Lease Agreement to take such actions as may be necessary
to include all Lease Payments in its annual budgets and to make the necessary annual appropriations for all
such Lease Payments subject to complete or partial abatement of such Lease Payments resulting from a
taking of the Leased Property (either in whole or in part) under the powers of eminent domain or resulting
from damage or loss of all or any portion of the Leased Property. All of the Authority’s right, title and
interest in and to the Lease Agreement (apart from certain rights to receive Additional Payments, as defined
therein, to the extent payable to the Authority and to indemnification), including the right to receive Lease
Payments under the Lease Agreement, are assigned to the Trustee for the benefit of Bondholders under the
Indenture.

For a summary of the Indenture, the Lease Agreement and the Site Lease, see “APPENDIX A - SUMMARY
OF PRINCIPAL LEGAL DOCUMENTS” herein.

In general, the City is required under the Lease Agreement to pay to the Authority specified amounts for
use and possession of the Leased Property which are calculated to be sufficient in both time and amount to
pay, when due, the principal of and interest on the Bonds. The City is also required to pay any taxes and
assessments levied on the Leased Property and all costs of maintenance and repair of the Leased Property.
Except for the Authority’s right, title and interest in and to the Lease Payments and otherwise to the Lease
Agreement which have been assigned to the Trustee, no funds or properties of the Authority or the City are
pledged to or otherwise liable for the Bonds (see “RISK FACTORS” herein).

The Leased Property will consist of various City properties described below. Pursuant to the terms of the

Development Services Building. The Development Services Building was constructed in 2001 and is part

Development. The building contains a variety of city offices with a central one-stop counter and lobby on
the first floor.

Approximately 94 joint-use parking spaces are available adjacent to and south of the building. The insured
value of the building is $9,537,853 and it is located on 2.5 acres of land at the northwest corner of Sierra
Highway and Avenue Q-11.

Office Building. This building is also part of the Civic Center complex of buildings. The 18,000 square
foot office building was originally constructed in 2000 to serve as a County satellite courthouse. It now
serves as overflow space for City offices on an as-needed basis. The insured value of the building is
$4,780,156 and it is located on .86 acres of land.

 Work Force Development Center. The City owns an approximate 10,000 square foot office building
located on 0.7 acres at the corner of Sierra Highway and Avenue Q-6, with an adjacent 0.7 acres of parking.

Public Works Yard. The City’s Public Works Yard houses the City’s maintenance operations and

General Provisions
The Bonds will be issued in the form of fully registered Bonds in the principal amount of $5,000 each or
any integral multiple thereof. Interest on the Bonds is payable at the rates per annum set forth on the inside
front cover pages hereof, each June 1, 2024 and December 1, commencing June 1, 2024 (each, an “Interest
Payment Date”) until maturity. Interest on the Bonds will be computed on the basis of a 360-day year of
twelve 30-day months. Principal on the Bonds is payable on June 1 in each of the years and in the amounts
set forth on the inside front cover pages hereof.

Each Bond shall be dated as of the Closing Date and shall bear interest from the Interest Payment Date next
preceding the date of authentication thereof, unless (a) it is authenticated after the 15th day of the month
preceding an Interest Payment Date (each, a “Record Date”) and on or before the following Interest
Payment Date, in which event it shall bear interest from such Interest Payment Date, or (b) unless it is
authenticated on or before May 15, 2024, in which event it shall bear interest from the Closing Date;
provided, however, that if, as of the date of authentication of any Bond, interest thereon is in default, such
Bond shall bear interest from the Interest Payment Date to which interest has previously been paid or made
available for payment thereon.

Interest on the Bonds shall be payable to the person whose name appears on the Registration Books as the
Owner thereof as of the Record Date immediately preceding each such Interest Payment Date, such interest
to be paid by check of the Trustee mailed on such Interest Payment Date by first class mail to the Owners

   SOURCES OF PAYMENT FOR THE BONDS
General
The Bonds are payable from and secured by a pledge of Revenues and certain funds and accounts
established and held by the Trustee under the Indenture. Revenues, as defined in the Indenture, means:

  (a) all Lease Payments, prepayments, insurance proceeds, condemnation proceeds, and

  (b) subject to the provisions of the Indenture, all interest, profits or other income derived from the
  investment of amounts in any fund or account established pursuant to the Indenture, other than the
  Costs of Issuance Fund.

Revenues include Net Proceeds, which are amounts derived by the City from any policy of casualty
insurance with respect to any portion of the Leased Property, or the proceeds of any taking of the Leased
Property or any portion thereof in eminent domain proceedings (including sale under threat of such
proceedings), to the extent remaining after payment therefrom of all expenses incurred in the collection and
administration thereof. See “Insurance Relating to the Leased Property” below.

As security for the Bonds, the Authority will assign to the Trustee for the payment of the Bonds the
Authority’s rights, title and interest in the Lease Agreement (with certain exceptions), including the right to
receive Lease Payments to be made by the City under the Lease Agreement.

The Bonds are limited obligations of the Authority payable solely from and secured by a pledge of Revenues
and certain funds and accounts held under the Indenture. The Authority has no taxing power.

Lease Payments; Abatement
The City is required to pay the Lease Payments to the Authority for use of the Leased Property, which are
equal to the principal of and interest due with respect to the Bonds. The Lease Agreement requires the City
to make Lease Payments to the Authority at least 5 business days preceding each Interest Payment Date.
Lease Payments to be paid by the City are assigned to the Trustee under the Indenture and are to be
transmitted by the City directly to the Trustee. The Indenture provides that the Lease Payments will be
deposited in the Revenue Fund maintained by the Trustee under the Indenture and applied to pay the
principal of and interest on the Bonds.

The City has covenanted in the Lease Agreement to take such action as may be necessary to include all
Lease Payments in its annual budgets and to make annual appropriations for all such Lease Payments. The
Lease Agreement provides that the several actions required by such covenants are deemed to be and shall
be construed to be duties imposed by law and that it is the duty of each and every public official of the City
to take such action and do such things as are required by law in the performance of the official duty of such
official to enable the City to carry out and perform the covenants in the Lease Agreement agreed to be
carried out and performed by the City.

California law requires, and the Lease Agreement provides, that the Lease Payments may be abated in
whole or in part if portions of the Leased Property are destroyed, damaged or condemned. During any
period in which by reason of damage or destruction (other than by eminent domain which is described
below) there is substantial interference with the use and occupancy by the City of the Leased Property or
any portion thereof, the Lease Payments are subject to abatement in an amount determined by the City such
that the resulting Lease Payments represent fair consideration for the use and occupancy of the remaining
usable portions of the Leased Property not damaged or destroyed. Such abatement will continue for the
period commencing with such damage or destruction and ending with the substantial completion of the
work of repair or reconstruction. In the event of any such damage or destruction, the Lease Agreement
continues in full force and effect and the City waives any right to terminate the Lease Agreement by virtue

  16
 of any such damage and destruction. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Lease Payments are not subject
to abatement to the extent that rental interruption insurance Net Proceeds are available to pay Lease
Payments that would otherwise be abated, it being hereby declared that such amounts constitute special
funds for the payment of the Lease Payments.

If the Leased Property is taken permanently under the power of eminent domain or sold to a government
threatening to exercise the power of eminent domain, the Lease Agreement will cease as of the day
possession is taken. If less than all of the Leased Property is taken permanently, or if the Leased Property
is taken temporarily, under the power of eminent domain, then (a) the Lease Agreement shall continue in
full force and effect with respect thereto and does not terminate by virtue of such taking, and the parties
waive the benefit of any law to the contrary; and (b) the Lease Payments are subject to abatement in an
amount determined by the City such that the resulting Lease Payments represent fair consideration for the
use and occupancy of the remaining usable portions of the Leased Property. However, that the Lease
Payments are not subject to abatement to the extent that rental interruption insurance Net Proceeds are
available to pay Lease Payments that would otherwise be abated, it being declared in the Indenture that
such amounts constitute special funds for the payment of the Lease Payments.

During any period of abatement of Lease Payments, the Trustee shall pay principal and interest on the
Bonds allocable to such portions of the Leased Property from proceeds of insurance or condemnation award
(if any) on a pro-rata basis. The reduced Lease Payments may not be sufficient to pay principal and interest
on the Bonds in the amounts and at the rates set forth therein. The City’s reduced Lease Payments will
constitute the total Lease Payments. In the event and to the extent the Lease Payments and other amounts
available to the Trustee under the Indenture are subject to abatement, there could be insufficient amounts
to pay principal of and interest on the Bonds in full, and such insufficiency would not constitute a default
by the City under the Indenture, the Lease Agreement or otherwise.

The term of the Lease Agreement commences on the Closing Date and will terminate on June 1, 2053, or
such earlier or later date on which the Lease Payments are paid in full or provisions made for such payment,
but in no event later than June 1, 2063, being ten years after the stated maturity date of the Bonds. The
Bonds are limited obligations of the Authority payable solely from and secured by a pledge of Revenues
and certain funds and accounts held under the Indenture.

The Authority has no taxing power. The obligation of the City to pay Lease Payments does not constitute
an obligation for which the City is obligated to levy or pledge any form of taxation or for which the City
has levied or pledged any form of taxation. The obligation of the City to pay Lease Payments does not
constitute a debt of the City, the State of California or of any political subdivision thereof within the
meaning of any constitutional or statutory debt limitation or restriction.

The City has other obligations payable from its General Fund and may enter into other obligations payable
from its General Fund without the consent of the Bond Owners. To the extent the City issues such

Reserve Account
A Reserve Account has been established under the Indenture to be held by the Trustee to secure the timely
payment of principal of and interest on each series of the Bonds. The Reserve Requirement for the Bonds
a fixed amount equal to the least of (a) maximum annual debt service on the Bonds, (b) 125% of average
annual debt service on the Bonds, and (c) 10% of the par amount of the Bonds; provided, however, that if
the Bonds are partially refunded, such amount shall be reduced to an amount equal to the maximum annual
debt service on the Bonds following such redemption.

 All amounts on deposit in the Reserve Account shall be used and withdrawn by the Trustee solely for the
purpose of making transfers to the Revenue Fund in the event of any deficiency at any time in such fund of

The Reserve Account established for the Bonds secures only the Bonds, and does not secure any other series

The Authority is not required under the Indenture to replace the Reserve Policy with cash or a replacement

   CITY OF PALMDALE
General Information
The City is located in northern Los Angeles County, in an area known as the Antelope Valley, approximately
62 miles north of downtown Los Angeles. It encompasses approximately 104 square miles. The southern
portion of the Antelope Valley is significantly urbanized and focused around the City and its neighboring
community, the City of Lancaster. Nearly half of the Antelope Valley’s population lives in these two cities
and are connected to the metropolitan employment center of the Los Angeles Basin via the Antelope Valley
Freeway (State Highway 14) and Interstate 5. Access to the Inland Empire (Riverside and San Bernardino
Counties) from Palmdale is via State Highway 18.

In 1933, the United States government established Muroc Air Base six miles north of Lancaster in Kern
County, now known as Edwards Air Force Base. The United States government also bought Palmdale
Airport in 1952 and established an aerospace development and testing facility called United States Air Force
Plant 42. One year later, in 1953, Lockheed established a facility at the airport. After this point in time,
the aerospace industry took over as the primary local source of employment, where it has remained ever
since. Today the City is even referred to as the “Aerospace Capital of America” because of its rich heritage
in being the home of many of the aircraft used in the United States military.

Government Organization
The City was incorporated as a general law city on August 24, 1962, and became a charter city in 2009.
The City operates under the council/manager form of government. The City is governed by a five-member
council elected by geographic districts. The Mayor is selected annually from among the City Council
members. The positions of City Manager and City Attorney are filled by appointments of the City Council.

Governmental Services
Public Safety and Welfare

Full-service law enforcement is provided to the residents of the City through a contractual arrangement
with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. Under the contract, the City is currently served by __
full-time equivalent sworn officers.

Fire protection and emergency medical services are provided in the City by Los Angeles County
Consolidated Fire Protection District, a fire prevention and suppression organization that serves 58 cities
and towns and the unincorporated areas of the County.

The City also contracts with the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control for animal
licensing, pickup, care, and boarding at a local shelter.

Public Services

City services include building permit and inspection, planning and zoning, public infrastructure
maintenance, street cleaning, traffic signal maintenance and municipal code compliance. Utilities in the
City are provided by separate utility companies, but the City maintains all sewer assets.

The City operates the Palmdale Transportation Center, a mulitmodal regional transportation center, which
offers connections between the Antelope Valley Transit Authority the following commuter services: Amtrak
Throughway Bus Service, Commuter Bus Service, FlixBus, Metrolink Commuter Rail Service, and Santa
Clarita Transit.

  21
 The City also offers various emergency services and opportunities to low-to moderate-income families and
individuals in securing affordable housing. To accomplish this, the City’s Community Programs
Department oversees the South Valley WorkSource Center, the Federal Home Program, the Community
Development Block Grant Program, the Neighborhood Stabilization Program, the Homelessness
Prevention and Rapid Re-housing Program, and the South Antelope Valley Emergency Service Program.

Parks and Recreation

The City operates the Palmdale Library. The City’s Department of Parks and Recreation manages the
operation of 592 acres of developed parkland throughout the City. The department also operates special
use facilities and developed trails and pathways. Facilities include four pools, a 6-acre water park, 12,000
capacity outdoor amphitheater, and numerous ball fields, tennis courts, basketball courts, skate parks, roller
hockey rinks, as well as three community centers and a community theatre.

Community Information
The City is served by two separate elementary school districts, Palmdale School District and Westside
Union School District, and one high school district, the Antelope Valley Union High School District. The
Palmdale Aerospace Academy is a joint venture between the City, the AERO Institute, and the Palmdale
School District. It is an independent charter school.

Nearby Antelope Valley College offers associates of arts and science degrees in multiple fields. Certificate
programs are offered in numerous vocational areas. Four-year degree programs are offered in the Antelope
Valley at satellite campuses of Chapman University, University of Antelope Valley, University of La Verne,
University of Phoenix, California State University at Bakersfield, California State Polytechnic University
at Pomona and California State University at Fresno.

Residents in the region are served by the Palmdale Regional Medical Center, a first class acute-care hospital
and medical center. The facilities include an emergency department, a helipad, medical office towers, and
a senior housing complex.

Transportation
The Antelope Valley Freeway (State Highway 14) is a north-south freeway that runs through the City and
provides access to Interstate 5 and the Southern California freeway system to the south, and State Highway
18 provides access to Interstate 15 to the east, connecting with the Inland Empire and Las Vegas. State
Highway 138, north of the City also connects with Interstate 5.

The City also operates the Palmdale Transportation Center described above.
